definitions.explanation: A projectile fired from a cannon or artillery piece. Also used more broadly for any large-caliber ammunition.

examples.japanese: {砲弾|ほうだん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{飛|と}んで→飛ぶ：00759_tobu⟧きた。
{不発弾|ふはつだん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{砲弾|ほうだん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{工事現場|こうじげんば}→工事現場：26202_koujigenba⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{見|み}つかった→見つかる：01173_mitsukaru⟧。
examples.english: An unexploded shell was found at the construction site.

examples.japanese: ⟦{戦時中|せんじちゅう}→戦時中：28629_senjichuu⟧、⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{何百発|なんびゃっぱつ}⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{砲弾|ほうだん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{撃|う}ち{込|こ}まれた。
examples.english: During the war, hundreds of shells were fired into this town.

notes: Composed of {砲|ほう} (cannon, artillery) + {弾|だん} (bullet, projectile). Common collocations: {砲弾|ほうだん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{着弾|ちゃくだん}→着弾：24807_chakudan⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (a shell lands/hits), {砲弾|ほうだん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{撃|う}ち{込|こ}む (to fire shells into), {砲弾|ほうだん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧ (a rain of shells). In Japan, {不発弾|ふはつだん} (unexploded ordnance) from World War II are still occasionally found during construction, especially in Okinawa. The counter for shells is ⟦{発|はつ}→〜発：04026_hatsu⟧: ⟦{一発|いっぱつ}→一発：08895_ippatsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{砲弾|ほうだん} (one shell).
